rule_and_citation.decision: REFUSE (same typed error as constant curves), not an invented monotonic-envelope inverse
rule_and_citation.icc: ICC.1:2022-05 (archive.color.org/specification/ICC.1-2022-05.pdf, printed page = PDF page - 14): Annex F (normative) F.1 p.101: a one-dimensional non-constant curve is invertible if it is monotonically increasing or monotonically decreasing over its domain; special cases a) flat subdomain [x1, x2] mapped to y1 with x2 != 1 inverts to the highest x (x2), a flat subdomain whose end point is 1 inverts to the lowest x (x1); b) a y with no x in the domain of the inverse takes the closest y in the range of the curve. F.2 grayTRCTag and F.3 red/green/blueTRC p.101-102: if the TRC function is not invertible the behaviour of the inverse is undefined; a constant curve cannot be inverted. Clause 10.6 curveType p.48: table entries are not required to be monotonic, so a non-monotonic table is valid data (forward use defined); clause 10.18 p.70-71: parametric curve values outside [0, 1] are clipped
rule_and_citation.lcms2: Little-CMS master src/cmsgamma.c (fetched with WebFetch, summarized by the fetch model, snippets quoted from its answer): cmsReverseToneCurveEx has no refusal path for tables; Ascending = !cmsIsToneCurveDescending (first entry <= last entry only); GetInterval scans from the highest index down for an ascending table (lowest index up otherwise) and returns the first interval containing y, so a non-monotonic table inverts silently by scan order; collapsed intervals use Ascending ? y2 : y1 (the highest x for ascending tables, also at an end run, where F.1 a) says the lowest); y outside the table range reuses the last fitted line. Neither the standard nor lcms2 documents an 'envelope'; Prism differs from lcms2 on purpose (refusal; F.1 end-run rule)
rule_and_citation.why_not_tolerance: F.1 gives no tolerance and u16 table entries compare exactly; a table with one count against the direction is refused (tested); real profiles with measurement-noise reversals would be refused as destinations (not as sources); no test of the 155-test prism suite (corpus required), of the 65 interop-psd + develop dependents tests or of the synthetic fixtures converts to a non-monotonic destination table, so no existing expectation moved; whether a real-world profile with noisy tables exists is UNVERIFIED (no evidence either way in the corpus)
